rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 6 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1379, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FORFEITURE LAW, TO PROVIDE A FIXED PERCENTAGE OF THE VALUE OF FORFEITED PROPERTIES IN CORRUPTION CASES AS ADDITIONAL FUNDING FOR THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to be earmarked as additional funding to the Office of the Ombudsman, a share of thirty percent (30%) of the value of asset or property forfeited in favor of the State.
Proposes further that: 
“IF THE PROPERTY IS NOT IN CASH IT SHALL BE SOLD AT PUBLIC AUCTION AND THE PROCEEDS THEREOF, AFTER DEDUCTING THE THIRTY PERCENT (30%) FOR THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN, SHALL ACCRUE TO THE GENERAL FUND.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2020-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10149 OR THE GOCC GOVERNANCE ACT OF 2011
rows.abstract:
Proposes to rectify the overarching scope of R.A. 10149 which includes the compensation standardization of government officials and employees of GOCCs even without the original charter. 
Provides that non-chartered GOCCs created and organized under B.P. Blg.68 or the Corporation Code must be governed by the appropriate provisions of P.D. 442 or the Labor Code insofar as salary or compensation standardization is concerned.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2020-08-05

rows.author: H026
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 7, 10, 23, 30, 31, 42 AND 52 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE GSIS ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract:
Seeks to propose amendments in the GSIS Act of 1997 to redress the law´s ineffective implementation, particularly in responding to the needs of teachers who comprise the largest group in terms of membership in the GSIS.
Intends to recompense the improper computation of service including the charging of interests/surcharges/penalties on late remittances; to adjust coverage of benefits by GSIS to make them at par with the costs of living and the escalating inflation rate; and to enhance the law´s penalty clause to ensure that persons may be held accountable for prohibited acts committed.  Proposes to broaden the prerogative of concerned parties in the settlement of disputes covered by the law, by giving the RTC concurrent jurisdiction with the GSIS; and to increase the representation of the DepEd in the Board of Trustees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2020-08-05

rows.author: I028
rows.title_full:
AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE AUTONOMY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS,
AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 16 AND SECTION 41 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO.
7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991”
rows.abstract:
Intends to address LGU's limitation in the exercise of its powers brought about by national laws and policies that tend to prevent them from truly exercising their right to self-government and address the different needs of their constituents. Aims therefore, to further foster genuine and meaningful local autonomy by strengthening the delegated power of LGUs under Section 16 of the LGC, which embodies the general welfare clause.
Proposes that Section 41(b) of R.A. 7160, as amended by R.A.8553  is hereby further amended to read as follows:
“(b) The regular members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, and Sangguniang Bayan shall be elected by district as follows:
               “First and second-class provinces shall have NOT MORE THAN FOURTEEN (14) regular members; third and fourth-class provinces, NOT MORE THANT TWELVE (12); and fifth and sixth-class provinces, NOT MORE THAN TEN (10):  Provided, That, in provinces having more than five (5) legislative districts, each district shall have NOT MORE THAN THREE (3) Sangguniang Panlalawigan members.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2020-08-10

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROTECTING E-CONSUMERS AND E-MERCHANTS, CREATING FOR
THE PURPOSE THE E-COMMERCE BUREAU AND APPROPRIATING
FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to regulate the transactions and trade between e-merchant and e-consumer - to ensure fair business and advertising practices and to secure online transactions, especially the small and lowly platforms as follows: 
a) internet retail of consumer goods; b) online travel services; c) digital media providers; d) ride-hailing services, and e) financial services.
Proposes several provisions on business registration, online dispute resolution, and tax exemption, among others; States that only those whose generated revenue reach two hundred fifty thousand pesos (P250,000.00) shall be taxed.

rows.author: H056
rows.title_full:
AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10863 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE
"CUSTOMS MODERNIZATION AND TARIFF ACT"
rows.abstract:
Proposes to allow the BoC to utilize one percent (1%) of its annual income derived from its collection of customs duties and taxes for its modernization program.
Aims to give more leeway for the BoC to pursue seamless, efficient, and transparent trading procedures through the acquisition, upgrading, and modernization of equipment and information and technology equipment systems; and the construction, repair, and rehabilitation of its structures and facilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2020-08-11

rows.author: I089
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 8792 (ELECTRONIC COMMERCE ACT OF 2000), PROVIDING FOR STIFFER PENALTIES AND SANCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to facilitate domestic and international dealings, transactions, arrangements, agreements, contracts and exchanges and storage of information through the utilization of electronic, optical, and similar medium, mode, instrumentality, and technology to recognize the authenticity and reliability of electronic documents related to such activities and to promote the universal use of electronic transaction in the government and general public.
Proposes to amend Sec.33 of the Electronic Commerce Act of 2000 as regards to penalties by fine and/or imprisonment to acts of hacking or crackling; piracy;  violations of the Consumer Act and other relevant pertinent laws through transaction covered by or using electronic data messages or electronic documents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2020-08-11
